title: Arronix extension manifest
description: EDITOR AID ONLY. The runtime gate is Arronix.Plugins.Manifest.PluginManifestReader plus PluginManifestValidator, which read into required members with unmapped members disallowed. This document exists so an editor can offer completion; it is never consulted at load time and must not be treated as authoritative if the two ever disagree.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this manifest format. Only 1 is understood.

id.description: Lower-case alphanumeric segments separated by dots, starting with a letter.

name.description: The name shown to an operator.

version.description: The extension's own version, in Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 form.

description.description: An optional sentence describing what the extension is for.

contracts.description: The contract versions the extension declares it works against.

arronix.description: The compatible plugin-consumable Arronix.Abstractions SDK range, in a documented subset of npm/yarn syntax: comparison operators, whitespace conjunction, '||' alternation and partial versions. Caret, tilde, wildcards and hyphen ranges are rejected.

entryAssembly.description: The bare file name of the assembly holding the single IPluginModule, when the package carries executable behavior. Resolved inside the extension's own folder; separators and parent-directory segments are rejected. A package may declare zero or one. A package that declares none must publish at least one contract assembly and must declare no capability, because it runs no code of its own.

contractAssemblies.description: The bare file names of the assemblies this package publishes for its dependants to bind against. Zero or more, resolved inside the package's own folder, compared case-insensitively for duplicates, and never the entry assembly: shared contract types and executable plugin code have different isolation, update and unload lifetimes.

clientContracts.description: The subset of contractAssemblies a browser client may download and load. Zero or more, each of which must also appear in contractAssemblies: a client receives the same admitted CLR identity a dependant binds to, or nothing. Never the entry assembly, which cannot be a shared contract assembly in the first place. Declared rather than inferred, because whatever is named here leaves the host's process and is readable by anyone the client is served to.

dependencies.description: The packages this one requires. One edge per required package: an exact identifier and one compatible version range. Requiring a package grants its shared contract assemblies and, when it carries executable behavior, requires that exact package to be admitted first. Direct edges only; the transitive closure is derived.

package.description: The exact identifier of the required package. Never this package's own.

range.description: The compatible versions of it, in the same range grammar as contracts.arronix. A predicate against the one installed version, never a selector among several.

capabilities.description: The privileges the extension declares. Enforcement is bidirectional: a declared capability must have a matching registration, and a gated registration must have a declared capability. A package with an entry assembly must declare at least one; a package without one must declare none.

mediaKinds.description: A transitional declaration of media kinds for legacy shape-based extensions. It requires the 'media-kind' capability when present. Typed media extensions omit it because Host derives their kinds from the admitted definition; holding the capability does not require an entry here.

identifiers.description: A transitional, non-authoritative external-identifier inventory for legacy extensions. Typed media owns identity roles, while each installed cataloger contributes the schemes and release markers it owns.

tokens.description: A transitional naming-token inventory for legacy extensions. Typed media omits it because Host derives tokens from the prepared kind. When present, names are compared by their invariant-lowercased alphanumeric grammar identity and must agree exactly with the prepared or legacy shape. A bare string is accepted and widened to a descriptor with an empty description.

policies.description: A transitional policy inventory for legacy extensions. Typed media omits it because policy is compiled from typed declarations. The validator currently checks the closed category shape plus nonblank, unique identifiers; it does not treat this list as executable policy authority.
